title: Understanding the origins of the mutational landscape in cancer
text:
Exposure to environmental genotoxins constitutes a significant risk factor for cancer development, with cancers
bearing mutational signatures indicative of these environmental exposures. Moreover, internal processes also
play a role in shaping these signatures. This proposed project seeks to advance our understanding of both
internal processes and external environmental exposures in generating mutational signatures that contribute to
cancer development.

title: Parallel training in human and animal studies to evaluate the effects of age-related changes to extended high frequency sensitivity and cognition on higher-order auditory processing
text:
Degraded speech-in-noise performance has been associated with both elevated extended high frequency
hearing thresholds and cognitive decline. Measurement of the extended high frequencies may provide clinical
value in relation to speech perception in the presence of background noise and has not been studied in reference
to the correlation between hearing loss and cognitive decline. Our proposed research involves parallel human
and animal model studies evaluating the role of extended high frequency hearing, speech-in-noise performance,
and biomarker changes for cognitive decline.

title: CaNCURE:  Cancer Nanomedicine Co-ops for Undergraduate Research Experiences
text:
CaNCURE: Cancer Nanomedicine Co-ops for Undergraduate Research Experiences

This renewal of the CaNCURE: Cancer Nanomedicine Co-ops for Undergraduate Research Experiences Program seeks to provide training and education in research at the interface of nanotechnology, cancer biology, and medicine in order to attract, retain, and encourage young scientists & engineers to pursue careers in cancer research.  The program will achieve this central aim by creating meaningful and rigorous research experiences mentored by outstanding academic and clinical researchers and supplemented with various other learning and professional development opportunities. The program combines Northeastern University’s co-op model of education with outstanding cancer nanomedicine research infrastructure at Dana-Farber / Harvard Cancer Center to create an immersive training environment for knowledge and skills acquisition.

title: CACHET - Environmental Biomarkers Core
text: 1. ENVIRONMENTAL BIOMARKERS CORE (EBC): ABSTRACT The overall goal of the Environmental Biomarkers Core (EBC) is to provide bioanalytical services in support of ChicAgo Center for Health and EnvironmenT (CACHET) members conducting environmental health research at the University of Chicago (UofC) and University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC). By providing the necessary experimental expertise to assess a wide range of environmental biomarkers, the EBC directly contributes to CACHET’s mission to improve environmental health outcomes within our communities. Toward that end, the EBC consists of two complimentary Sub-Cores: 1) a mass spectrometry-based Environmental Exposures Sub- Core that is P30-specific in services and resources available to members, and 2) a Biomarkers of Exposure Effects and Susceptibility Sub-Core that leverages existing institutional resources at UofC and UIC and streamlines services to members. The P30-specific Environmental Exposures Sub-Core at UIC will use mass spectrometry to assess toxic chemicals, heavy metals and metalloids, herbicides, pesticides, perfluoroalkyl substances, steroids and DNA oxidation products, among others, in both biological and environmental samples. New assays for environmental compounds will be developed and validated as needed by CACHET investigators. The Biomarkers of Exposure Effects and Susceptibility Sub-Core will leverage established institutional strengths in microbiome sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, genomics, epigenomics and transcriptomics on the two campuses. Further, bioinformatics support for all CACHET PI-initiated research projects and Facility Core activities will be provided from established institutional cores at both partner institutions. For all of these services, CACHET members will enjoy priority access and subsidized rates for environmental health research projects provided by Center resources and leveraging institutional cost-sharing of intellectual expertise, management platforms and heavy investments in high-end instrumentation. These combined resources help address the EBC mission to provide qualitative and quantitative data regarding biomarkers of exposure, disease and therapeutic responses as well as levels of environmental contaminants in human subjects, model systems and environmental samples at subsidized rates and with priority access to Center members.

title: Elucidating Tumor Cell CTGF-TGF-b Signaling Axis in driving Pancreatic Cancer Cachexia
text:
Cancer cachexia, which effects up to 50% of all individuals with cancer and highly prevalent in pancreatic cancer, is a disease characterized by dysmetabolism and systemic inflammation that ultimately results in body wasting primarily attributed to skeletal muscle loss, with or without the loss of fat mass. Cachexia negatively impacts patient outcomes as these individuals have a decreased quality of life and physical function, decreased tolerance and increased toxicity to cancer killing treatments, and greatly decreases survival.
Despite this, there are no current U.S. approved therapies to combat cachexia. In the current grant, I will investigate connective tissue growth factor (CTGF/CCN2) in the regulation of TGF-B signaling intratumorally and systemically, in driving cachexia and muscle pathophysiology.

title: The RCMI Program in Health Disparities at Meharry Medical College - Supplement
text:
Social determinants of health (SDoH) are connected with low self-esteem, self-efficacy, and failed attempts at
substance use disorder (SUD) abstinence. Collecting and integrating SDoH information as part of patients’
electronic health records (EHR) for clinical modeling could help uncover health disparities, patient experiences
and behaviors related to SUD. In this proposal, we will to address the challenge of SDoH extraction and SUDs
identification from unstructured clinical notes or patient surveys by developing two natural language processing
(NLP) pipelines, and build SUD prediction models integrating the SDoH associated factors and SUD diagnosis
that will be obtained from the two NLP pipelines, along with other phenotype risk factors being extracted from
EHR structured data.

title: Development of Manufacturing Controls for ORL1: A Fluorescent Imaging Agent for In Vivo Molecular Imaging of Melanomas
text:
This project aims to develop and manufacture ORL1, a fluorescent imaging agent used in the Skin Fluorescent
Imaging (SFI) System, to enhance the early detection of melanoma by imaging proteins expressed in
developing melanomas. By improving clinical diagnostic accuracy and reducing unnecessary biopsies, ORL1
has the potential to significantly improve patient outcomes and modernize melanoma care.

title: Developing Improved Reporter Mouse Models for In Vivo Gene Editing
text:
Gene editing therapy is an emerging medical approach in which a specific portion of a patient’s DNA is
changed to treat, or perhaps even cure, an underlying genetic illness. Among the most promising of these
approaches, known as base editing, allows precise DNA modification without some of the drawbacks of other
gene editing approaches. The goals of this proposal/project are to create two specialized strains of laboratory
mice that can be used by the scientific community to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of various base editing
therapies.

title: Reinvigorating the overdominant model of tumor suppression
text:
Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, yet our
understanding of tumor suppressor loss in lung cancer is still limited. This project will combine
advanced CRISPR-Cas9 techniques, sophisticated mouse models, and barcode sequencing
innovations with comprehensive in vivo and molecular analyses to study the overdominant tumor
suppression in lung adenocarcinoma. Understanding this specific mechanism of tumor
suppression will be instrumental in developing more effective therapeutic strategies.

title: Computational methods to interpret genomic variation and integrate functional genomics data in genetic analysis of human diseases
text:
Accurate and scalable interpretation of genomic variation is a critical component to realize the full potential of
high-throughput sequencing in human genetics and genomic medicine. My lab is focused on developing new
computational methods to predict functional impact of genomic variation and to integrate multi-modal genomic
data sets in genetic analysis by machine learning. These methods will improve the utility of genome sequencing
and functional genomics data and enable new discoveries in genetic studies of human diseases and clinical
diagnosis.

title: Advancing manufacturing and release testing of a gene editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy
text:
Manufacturing optimization and analytics are required to have in place before production of cGMP
material for clinical trials. This project will perform manufacturing and release testing optimization
for a dual AAV vector gene editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. This work is critical
for advancing development of this therapy that can restore dystrophin for 50% of all Duchenne
patients.

title: The hypoxic niche in glioblastoma is maintained by myeloid produced creatine
text:
Glioblastoma is the most common and aggressive primary brain tumor in adult which is defined by a hypoxic
niche that drives resistance to therapies and promotes tumor growth. Our data indicates this niche is fueled by
creatine delivered by infiltrating immune cells. In this proposal we seek to understand the role of creatine in
promoting GBM growth and if creatine metabolic inhibition is a useful strategy by which we can hinder GBM
growth and recurrence.

title: Core B: Translational, Cellular and Molecular Analysis
text:
Core B's experimental processing services will determine the cellular and genomic features defining high risk 
gastric precursors. The core will support experimental models to define the underlying biology. By providing a 
range of sophisticated imaging, molecular and sequencing assays, the core will streamline the progress of the 
Program Project Grant and its goal of advancing precision cancer detection.

title: Defining and perturbing gene regulatory dynamics in the developing human brain
text:
This project aims to understand both how complex neuronal tissues differentiate during human development and
how genetic variation can affect this process by studying two highly medically relevant, in vitro, temporally
dynamic differentiation systems that faithfully recapitulate fetal differentiation patterns of the brain. For each of
these differentiation systems, we will carry out aims that span efforts toward mapping, perturbing, modeling,
validating, and learning from single cell derived molecular data sets, with a goal of learning DNA sequence
elements that drive gene expression programs during developmental timepoints. This understanding will provide
mechanistic insight into how DNA sequence elements cooperate to bring about cell state and fate changes and
help identify the genetic determinants of diseases of the brain.

title: Advancing Systematic Delivery of Oncolytic Adenovirus for Pancreatic Cancer
text:
The goal of this proposal is to develop a new swine model of pancreatic cancer to enable preclinical testing
of systemically delivered oncolytic adenoviruses to detect and treat pancreatic cancer. Successful products from
this proposal can be promptly translated to the clinical arena bringing novel therapeutic approaches to the
patients with pancreatic cancer including those with unresectable metastatic disease.

title: Huntsman Cancer Institute (HCI) Cancer Genetics, Epigenetics, Models, and Signaling (Cancer GEMS) Training Program
text:
The Huntsman Cancer Institute (HCI) Cancer Genetics, Epigenetics, Models, and Signaling (Cancer GEMS)
Training Program will support six PhD candidates each year. Students will participate in a two-year training
program consisting of a combination of mentored research, didactic courses, career development activities,
seminars, and conferences, all aimed at preparing these young scientists for the next stage of their careers in
cancer research. This program will produce a cadre of new scientists capable of working with physicians to
develop improved and individualized methods of cancer prevention, early detection/interception, and treatment.

title: Early Epigenetic Drivers of Revival Stem Cell Emergence in Intestinal Injury
text:
Radiation therapy for abdominal and pelvic cancers frequently causes intestinal injury, leading to chronic
gastrointestinal dysfunction with no targeted treatments available. The molecular mechanisms that govern early
regenerative responses, particularly the emergence of intestinal revival stem cells (RevSCs), remain poorly
understood. This project applies single-nucleus multi-omics, enhancer mapping, animal and intestinal organoid
models to define how chromatin remodeling and CBP/p300 activity regulate RevSC formation and intestinal
epithelial regeneration.

title: Epigenetic and metabolic mechanisms of environmentally-induced transgenerational germline dysfunction
text:
While in utero ethanol exposure causes a well-described complex of conditions, there is also
mounting evidence and concerns that some outcomes, including reproductive outcomes, are
also detectable in the third generation following initial exposure. However, how a memory of
ethanol exposure is initiated and then transmitted to future generations is currently not well
understood. Our work will identify the epigenetic and metabolic underpinnings of ethanol’s
transgenerational reproductive effects which will lay out a strong foundation for the implication of
these pathways in a human context.

title: Imaging Cancer Heterogeneity with High-Fidelity MRI
text: (TR&D1: Imaging Cancer Heterogeneity with High- Fidelity MRI) Technology Research and Development 1 (TR&D 1) focuses on the development of advanced quantita- tive MRI techniques – speciﬁcally diﬀusion and chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) imaging – to support initial diagnosis, preoperative imaging, intervention guidance, and treatment monitoring. The proposed innovations aim to enable robust, high-resolution imaging and derivation of reproducible, quantitative and thus multi-site comparable imaging biomarkers with immediate translational potential. Diﬀusion imaging based on conventional single-shot echo-planar imaging trails other established imaging contrasts in spatial resolution, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and geometric ﬁdelity. To address this, we pro- pose a novel motion-compensated, multi-shot single-slab 3D diﬀusion imaging sequence implemented on a high-performance head-only 3T MRI system, but ultimately also realizable on the latest generation of high performance whole-body systems. This approach allows for unprecedented isotropic high-resolution imaging with improved spatial ﬁdelity at scan times that are practical in a clinical setting. To overcome inconsistencies in apparent diﬀusion coeﬃcient (ADC) quantiﬁcation, we introduce a robust ﬁtting frame- work that yields consistent ADC values over the entire imaging volume and for diﬀerent protocols and scanner types. A major advantage of the proposed approach, which will be investigated, is the ability to combine the acquisition of basic high SNR ADC diﬀusion metrics with advanced diﬀusion metrics that can yield high resolution ﬁber maps or more detailed information about cell architecture, i.e., information that is highly relevant for preoperative assessment and intervention guidance. For CEST imaging, TR&D 1 ad- dresses a critical translational bottleneck: scanner-dependent bias. We present a harmonization framework based on temperature-stabilized phantoms, vendor-neutral Pulseq sequences, and automated optimization to minimize inter-scanner variability in contrasts that are sensitive for the presence of tumor-speciﬁc pro- teins. All of these tools support standardization across platforms, paving the way for AI models trained on harmonized data, thus enabling more reliable preoperative assessment and robust early response biomark- ers for treatment monitoring. The proposed developments will primarily be evaluated in brain tumor patients scheduled for their ﬁrst surgical intervention, but potential translation to other organs will be as- sessed in the prostate of normal subjects. Together, these eﬀorts advance TR&D 1’s mission of delivering reproducible, high-resolution, and clinically actionable imaging tools for optimal preoperative assessment and guidance during intervention. The tools, protocols, and data pipelines developed will be disseminated, fostering multi-center research and further development.

title: Elucidating Mechanism of Cardiac Fibrosis with Cell Village of Pooled Human iPSCs
text:
Cardiac fibrosis contributes to the progression of heart failure, but there is no FDA-approved drug specifically
targeting cardiac fibrosis due to the lack of understanding of the underlying mechanism and a reliable drug
discovery platform. This proposal will leverage state-of-the-art iPSC biology, tissue engineering, animal
models, and single-cell multiome analyses to elucidate the underlying mechanisms for cardiac fibrosis. We
expect to identify new treatments for patients with cardiac fibrosis and heart failure which is an unmet need.
